anita (sec-oncall): Alert: spike of SSO sessions for jordan@redwood.ai from two geo locations within 7 minutes. SIEM shows Chile -> Northern VA.

luca (identity): Seeing same. SAML InResponseTo mismatch on the second assertion for that user. RelayState blank.

sam (sre): What IPs? any shared ASN or known VPN exit nodes?

anita (sec-oncall): IPs: 200.45.12.9 (CL), 34.120.45.11 (us-east1). ASN for first is LATAM-ISP-1. Second resolves to Google Cloud.

maya (sec): MFA logs show push accepted on the US login, but the device fingerprint doesn't match previous device list. Could be MFA fatigue or social engineering.

luca (identity): Quick check: the SAML connector cert rotated 3 days ago, KMS record shows successful sign operation. Not seeing private key compromise signs. Still, InResponseTo mismatch suggests replayer or proxy.

anita (sec-oncall): Immediate containment proposals: 1) Revoke all active sessions for jordan across all devices. 2) Force reauth + password reset. 3) Block 34.120.45.11 for auth traffic for 1hr. Thoughts?

sam (sre): Agree. I'll run session-revoke for the user and block the IP at the WAF layer. Command: `authctl revoke-sessions --user jordan@redwood.ai --all` and `gcloud compute firewall-rules update deny-auth --add-src-ranges 34.120.45.11/32`

luca (identity): I'll pull full SAML request/response pair and check relaystate + audiences. Also will export the assertion raw and fingerprint it: `openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256 -in saml_cert.pem`

maya (sec): Can we also check if any admin console actions happened during the window? escalate to SOX?

anita (sec-oncall): No admin API calls from that user in the window. Only login events.

luca (identity): Found suspicious header: `X-Forwarded-For` present on the Chile request with a private IP. Could be a proxy chain. Also `AuthnContextClassRef` was `PasswordProtectedTransport` for the US event — MFA was step-up, but possibly bypassed due to cached session from a different IdP hop.

sam (sre): IP block applied, sessions revoked, WAF rule pushed. Deploy-bot: access-control change: `deny-auth` rule deployed at 16:07 UTC. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: session-revoke job started for jordan@redwood.ai (job id: 9f3b2c).

maya (sec): Next steps: initiate user outreach, confirm they initiated the login, and require scoped forensic snapshot of their workstation if they confirm they did not. Also add this to incident tracker.

anita (sec-oncall): Reached out to jordan via phone and Slack DM — they say they didn't log in from Chile. Marking as compromised.

luca (identity): For postmortem: 1) increase assertion validation strictness (reject InResponseTo mismatch), 2) add extra logging for RelayState and X-Forwarded-For for 90 days, 3) rotate SAML connector cert through KMS and add HSM-backed signing for production.

sam (sre): Operational wins: we revoked sessions quickly and blocked the IP. Need to confirm any service-to-service tokens minted during window. I'll grep token service logs: `grep "jordan@redwood.ai" /var/log/token-service/2026-03-20.log`

maya (sec): Also add automated detection rule: if same user authenticates from two geos within 15 minutes -> auto-suspend and page sec-oncall.

anita (sec-oncall): Thanks team. I'll file the incident, assign post-incident owner (luca), and schedule a blameless review tomorrow 09:30 PT.

luca (identity): Acknowledged. I'll prepare the SAML artifacts and a short runbook for stricter validation.

maya (sec): Add remediation: enforce reauth for all SSO sessions older than 30 days until we finish rollouts.

anita (sec-oncall): Last note: check KMS audit logs for any unusual signing requests around cert rotation time. luca, can you confirm?

luca (identity): Confirmed — KMS audit shows only expected rotation calls. No anomalies there.

anita (sec-oncall): closing thread for now, incident created: INC-2026-033, will attach logs and timeline.
